reforms.description: The August 1981 Economic Recovery Tax Act introduced a 25 percent tax credit for incremental research and development costs, reducing the effective cost of R&D investment for firms.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax credits reduce the cost of innovation investment, incentivizing private firms to increase research spending and develop new technologies, thereby raising productivity and long-term growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The text states 'A 25 percent credit for incremental research and development costs' under the August 1981 Economic Recovery Tax Act, indicating the measure was enacted into law.
reforms.importance_rationale: The R&D tax credit is a significant innovation instrument that directly reduces the cost of private-sector R&D investment. While not a structural overhaul of the innovation system, it represents a meaningful policy tool to incentivize applied research and development across industries.
reforms.source_quote: A 25 percent credit for incremental research and development costs.
